review_notes:
The target file contains a single theorem, `common_subsequence_compose`, with a four-line proof. It destructures the two hypotheses, applies `common_sublist_lower_bound` (from LCSCore.lean) to the two sublists of `y`, and closes the goal with `Sublist.trans` and `omega`. There is no second proof in this file that could repeat it.

I also searched the repository for related uses. `lcs_overlap` in LCS.lean (lines 76–82) follows the same pattern: two `obtain`s, a call to `common_sublist_lower_bound huy hvy`, then `trans` and `omega`. `sublist_survives_deletions` in LCSCore.lean and CodeTrimming.lean also call `common_sublist_lower_bound`. In every case, though, the shared part is a single lemma call plus trivial gluing. The nontrivial reasoning, the induction on `w`, already lives in one place: `common_sublist_lower_bound`.

Pulling the three-line glue into a new helper would only produce a thin wrapper around existing API, which the rubric says is not enough. `common_subsequence_compose` is itself that kind of wrapper, and `lcs_overlap` works with `lcs`/`exists_lcs` rather than the existential form, so rewriting it to use the target would save almost nothing. I found no repeated proof machinery that justifies a finding.
